rationale: A wins because it keeps the facts on a leash and turns them into different reportable stories, especially "What happens to the workers when Oatly shuts the plant" as a smart defensive angle founders usually miss. B has useful bones, but "customers who don't specify get oat milk" is a central fact error, not a spicy interpretation. Once an angle set starts freelancing on what "default" means, the rest needs adult supervision.
gaps_in_A: "Oatly launches its lowest-footprint product while closing a US plant" overclaims. The update says 31% lower than the previous formula, not Oatly's lowest-footprint product.
"verified per-liter number... is rarer than a self-reported one" is plausible but not in the supplied facts. Keep it as a reason for scrutiny, not a claim.
The green-premium angle needs outside evidence before it is pitchable; A asks for it, but the headline still assumes the consumer-price story is strong enough from one no-price-change fact.
gaps_in_B: "customers who don't specify get oat milk" is invented. The update says default non-dairy option, not default milk for every undecided customer.
"falling volumes, shrinking retail shelf space, canceled expansions" is unsupported category scenery. If you need market decline data, ask for it before making it the paragraph's spine.
"The plant closure and partnership are announced simultaneously" is not in the update. Current facts do not prove same announcement timing.

"Customer-story... no_journalist_shape" contradicts the kept chain-default angle. You cannot reject the customer lens for missing the chain name while also building your first angle around that same unnamed chain.
